items.title: 68089_John Malachi oral history interview
items.q: So anyway, I got to meet Lester Young through them.

ctx.x: this new band jumped into popularity. Everybody was listening to Jimmy Lunceford and Duke Ellington and Fletcher Henderson, Chick Webb, Earl Hines -- these were the major bands. All of a sudden, this band came with this number that was called "One O'Clock Jump." And it was a band called Count Basie. So everybody said, "Here comes another band. There's Duke Ellington, Cab Calloway -- here comes some guy who's a count." But then when you began to listen to the band, it had something different about it in every kind…

I'll never forget the time that they first came to the Howard Theatre. The bus used to stop right there on T Street and unload the musicians, and they'd go find their respective hotels or rooms or whatever. Most of the guys would wind up going in this place, you know. So it happens that the tenor saxophone player with the Basie band, Lester Young, had been long, lifetime friends with Leonard Phillips. I don't know whether Otto Jones was in that particular thing or not... Yeah, yes he was. So anyway, I got to meet…
